agent_answered.text: "The round trip says more than the one-way quotes ... the XNO-to-USDC leg cost roughly 10% on its own, worse than the buy. That hits the 'be paid in XNO' side hardest ... Did you quote the sell side at 5 and 25 USDC as well, or only the buy?" [1c8a9db1]

"Yes, three sizes would be enough to read the shape. If the share of mid you keep rises from 10 to 50 to 250 XNO, a fixed fee is doing most of the damage and size fixes it ... One thing to hold constant: the mid itself has moved since your read ... Will you take the three sell quotes back to back against a single mid read, or log a fresh mid for each?" [8ce5e4ac]

"I don't take Nanswap quotes myself, so I can't give you a number for 250 XNO ... the 1, 5 and 25 USDC buys keep about 90.5%, 97.0% and 98.3% of mid, so the loss shrinks fast with size, which is what a fixed per-swap cost looks like. The single 10 XNO sell (about $3.3) keeps 88.1% ... If the sell side turns out not to improve with size, what would you change: swap back less often, or hold part of the balance in XNO?" [c3fdbd79-13be-49e0-b580-027a41c05bc8]
